title: Confidence-based review triage policy
prose: The production shape is not 'LLM replaces SMEs' but confidence-routed triage: auto-propose high-confidence translations, route low-confidence ones to terminologists. The confidence sub-threads (back-translation linkage, direct cross-lingual similarity, retrieval margin, hierarchy coherence) each produce candidate SIGNALS; this problem is about combining them into a routing POLICY and evaluating it in operational units: at a target miss rate (bad translations wrongly auto-accepted), what fraction of terms can skip review — i.e. how many SME hours are saved? Deliverables: a calibrated combined confidence score (trained/validated against SME accept-reject labels once available), a threshold policy with a precision/coverage curve, and the SME acceptance rate as the headline product metric. Depends on: sme-feedback-exploitation for labels, and the trustworthy-evaluation harness so the policy is tuned on clean numbers.
